skill.name: snapdom
skill.description: snapDOM helps developers capture styled HTML elements and export them as SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP, Canvas, or Blob outputs.
skill.summary: Capture styled DOM elements and export them as reusable image assets.
skill.author: 2025Emma

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, inline option names, documented setup commands, and public resource links. No prompt injection, covert upload behavior, or hidden command execution was found. The only substantive risk is privacy exposure when users route captured page resources through a CORS proxy.

remediation.issue: CORS proxy guidance lacks a privacy warning.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to avoid third-party proxies for sensitive pages and to use a trusted same-origin or self-hosted proxy when proxy fallback is required.

remediation.issue: CDN import examples depend on remote package delivery.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend pinned package versions or npm installation for production use to reduce supply-chain and availability risk.

static_findings.snippet: | `width` | Number | Custom output width in pixels |
| `height` | Number | Custom output height in pixels |
| `useProxy` | String\|Boolean | Enable CORS proxy (URL or true for default) |
| `exclude` | String | CSS selector for elements to hide |
1. **Performance**: Use `scale` instead of `width`/`height` for better performance
2. **Fonts**: Set `embedFonts: true` to ensure custom fonts appear correctly
3. **CORS Issues**: Use `useProxy: true` if images fail to load
5. **Quality**: For PNG/JPG, use `quality: 0.95` for best quality
- Try `straighten: false` if transforms are causing issues
- **Orbit CSS Toolkit** - Companion toolkit by Zumerlab (https://github.com/zumerlab/orbit)

content.value_statement: Frontend teams often need accurate screenshots of styled components without a browser automation stack. This skill shows how to use snapDOM to export DOM elements as SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP, Canvas, or Blob outputs.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use snapDOM for DOM-to-image capture.
Shows npm, yarn, CDN module, and UMD installation options.
Provides examples for SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP, Canvas, and Blob exports.
Documents capture options for scale, dimensions, fonts, shadows, and exclusions.
Covers CORS fallback, plugin extension, troubleshooting, and performance guidance.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not include runnable helper scripts.
CORS proxy examples require careful trust and privacy review before use.
Browser rendering differences can affect final image output.
Large or complex captures may need tuning for performance and memory use.

use_cases.title: Export component previews
use_cases.description: Create reusable image assets from styled UI components for design reviews or documentation.

use_cases.title: Generate social images
use_cases.description: Capture fixed-size DOM layouts for cards, banners, and marketing previews.

use_cases.title: Compare rendering quality
use_cases.description: Evaluate SVG and raster outputs when building visual export workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a basic capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the simplest way to capture a DOM element with snapDOM and export it as a PNG.

prompt_templates.title: Tune output size and quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure snapDOM options for a high-resolution export with fixed width, fixed height, and good image quality.

prompt_templates.title: Handle missing fonts or resources
prompt_templates.prompt: My snapDOM capture is missing fonts and some images. Walk me through safe troubleshooting steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a custom export flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with exclusions and plugins.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a snapDOM workflow that excludes controls, embeds fonts, exports SVG and PNG, and leaves room for a PDF plugin.

output_examples.input: I need a sharp image of a styled chart for a product page.
output_examples.output: Use SVG export first because charts benefit from scalable vector output. Enable font embedding, wait for styles to load, and test the result across target browsers.

output_examples.input: My capture includes buttons that should not appear in the final image.
output_examples.output: Use an exclusion selector for controls or data attributes. Keep the selector narrow so important content is not removed from the capture.

output_examples.input: Images fail because they are loaded from another domain.
output_examples.output: Prefer same-origin assets when possible. If you use a proxy, choose a trusted proxy and avoid sending sensitive page resources through third parties.

best_practices: Wait for fonts, images, and CSS to finish loading before capturing.
Use SVG for charts and interface previews that need scalable output.
Use a trusted proxy only when same-origin resource handling is not possible.
anti_patterns: Do not capture sensitive user data into shareable images without review.
Do not send private page resources through an untrusted CORS proxy.
Do not use very high scale values on large elements without testing memory use.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you use snapDOM to capture HTML elements and export them as image formats or canvas data.

faq.question: Which image formats are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP, Canvas, and Blob outputs.

faq.question: Can it preserve styles and fonts?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers embedded styles, pseudo-elements, shadows, and optional font embedding.

faq.question: Does it include executable scripts?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed skill is documentation and examples. It does not include runnable automation files.

faq.question: Is CORS proxy use safe?
faq.answer: It can be safe with a trusted proxy, but it may expose resource URLs or content to that proxy.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Frontend developers, product engineers, and QA teams can use it for DOM capture and image export workflows.
